prompt:
A design-sprint storyboard drawn in Copic markers and black fineliner on white marker paper: three panels in a row, each with a short hand-lettered caption underneath. Panel 1: At home, a traveller holds a mailed card and reads how to get help. Card text: "Your China travel guide" Caption: Planning includes a human point of contact. Panel 2: At a help desk, the traveller shows the card and asks about their route. Sign text: "Ask about your trip" Caption: A person helps resolve a real planning question. Panel 3: In China, the traveller uses the card to find the same help point. Card text: "Help while travelling" Caption: Support continues after arrival.
Style: mostly white paper showing through, with light cool grey marker shading only where needed to separate planes — keep it airy. One warm orange accent on the key screen elements. Loose confident linework, a few visible marker streaks but not filled in. People are simple sketched figures with no facial detail. Any text on a screen, card or sign is short, legible and spelled exactly as given; captions are hand-lettered in neat block capitals. Feels like a real concept storyboard stuck on a workshop wall. No logos, no brand names, no watermark. The three panels and their captions fill the frame edge to edge, with only a slim paper margin.
